scope: Connect the SFT chapter to the post-training introduction, show how the loss denominator changes microbatch gradients, and specify FLAN's held-out-task protocol.

review.sources: Stanford CS336 lecture 15 slides 2–30, with varied FLAN outputs from slide 10; Wei et al., FLAN v5 §§2.1–2.3 and Fig. 1; Tülu 3 v5 §§4.2–4.3.2, Tables 11/14 and Fig. 5; Transformers gradient accumulation documentation; Lambert's Instruction Fine-Tuning chapter. Unchanged Berkeley and Self-Instruct material preserved.
review.workedCase: Two and eight SFT targets: naive weights 1/4 and 1/16 instead of 1/10 per token. Explicit sums 1 and 12 recover 1.3. The five targets of the chapter's small CPU Llama are divided 2+3, and the actual output matrix gradients test the exact weighted result against means-of-means. FLAN example uses the GPT chapter's same toy premise and hypothesis; no claim of new benchmark measurements.
review.provenance: Figure 5 original intact arXiv SVG; axes and line legend present. The archived Tülu v5 HTML establishes CC BY 4.0. FLAN Figure 1 is linked only; the arXiv copy lists a non-exclusive distribution grant rather than a reuse license.
review.limits: No GPU/full SFT training. The official Tülu sweep does not compare summed loss with an exact globally normalized average. EN remains labelled fallback. No push or deployment.
review.verification: Read the preceding 858-line owner in full, then the exact changes in context. All three published Python blocks and the new two-shard gradient comparison passed on CPU, PyTorch 2.14.1 and Transformers 4.57.1. Against the combined five-token loss, the correct reduction differed by 5.96e-8 in the output-weight gradient; the means-of-means control differed by 0.10425 in that run. Astro built 2099 pages. Chromium loaded all seven figures and no KaTeX errors in both locales at 375 and 1280 CSS px. Manually inspected the new graph, the worked calculation and the FLAN block; checked the source SVG and Stanford slide 10. Existing prose, exercises, and source anchors outside the edited sections were preserved.
